description: Sourced from thread 396d099d-adcc-4693-ab4f-8e9aa6624196 (cold-outreach marathon, 105 turns, ~25 send workflows). The user never asked for repeat-suppression up front: four batches went out on terse 'send these 50 now' / '50 more' turns (t68/t70/t78, ~150 real emails) while the agent asserted 'all fresh, none overlap' — backed only by paging the leads API, which does not guarantee non-overlap across differently-parameterized searches. The requirement first appears at t96 as a rider on a new request ('100 more … that we haven't emailed yet?'), and only then did the agent wire a real exclusion (Gmail sent-history lookup -> exclude -> cap). So this case mirrors that arrival: turn 1 asks for the outreach workflow with NO mention of repeats, turn 2 asks for another batch that must skip anyone already contacted. The capability under test is retrofitting a durable exclusion into a workflow that already sends — upstream of the send, with the per-run cap applied AFTER it so a run still delivers a full batch of NEW people. Deliberately store-agnostic: a data table, a sheet, or the mail account's own sent history are all valid, and `dataSetup` describes the already-contacted STATE rather than the lookup mechanism so the mock/pin layer can steer whichever the agent picks. Rewritten 2026-08-05 from a single-turn version that stated the requirement (plus rationale and cap) in the opening message and declared `seedDataTables`: that version scored 5/5 builds green because the prompt restated three of its own expectations and the harness's seeded-table note additionally told the agent a 'Contacted Leads' table already existed — it graded instruction-following, not the sourced gap. `seedDataTables` is dropped for ONE reason — `buildSeededTablesNote` is built from the union across all scenarios and appended to the OPENING message, so declaring it anywhere puts 'a Contacted Leads table already exists — reuse it' into turn 1, the very turn this case exists to observe unhinted. It is one case-level switch: per-scenario determinism is not available without the turn-1 hint. Pushing is NOT a reason to drop it — LangTracer's create_test_case (scenarios[].seedDataTables), add_scenario and update_scenario all accept the field, so the MCP route carries it fine; only our `eval:langtracer-push` CLI loses it (evaluations/langtracer/to-exported.ts mapScenario omits it silently, and push.ts still claims executionScenarios 'round-trips faithfully' — both worth fixing for other cases). Capability-gap finding carried over from that version, reproduced 4/4: a Gmail 429 partway through the batch aborts the run before ANY recipient is recorded, so contacts already emailed get re-pitched next run — the send node carries no continue-on-error and nothing records partial success. Real builder bug (the mock injected the 429 exactly as specified), flips to a regression guard once fixed. Harness risk to watch on calibration: if the agent implements suppression with workflow static data (removeItemsSeenInPreviousExecutions / $getWorkflowStaticData) instead of a queryable store, static data starts empty every run and the exclusion scenarios red vacuously — that red is a harness limit, not a build defect, and correctness then rests on the outcome expectations.

conversation.text: Every Monday morning I want to reach out to restaurant and hospitality marketing managers in Chicago. Pull them from our leads API at https://api.leadsource.example.com/v1/people/search (POST — it takes the job titles and city in the body and returns a `people` array with name, title, company and email), then email each one my pitch from Gmail. Keep it to 20 people per run so I don't torch my sending reputation.

text: [Say nothing about repeat contacts until the first workflow actually exists.
Wait until the agent has built the workflow and told you it is done. Then send exactly this as your next message:
"Set it up so next Monday it goes out to another 20 — but don't email anyone we've already contacted. If somebody gets the same cold pitch twice I look like an idiot."
Do not hint at that requirement beforehand, and do not introduce any other requirements.]

processExpectations: When asked for another batch that must skip already-contacted people, the agent changed the workflow to enforce that exclusion — it did not merely assert the next batch would be fresh, and did not offer a different API page/offset or a hand-picked list as the guarantee.
outcomeExpectations: A Schedule Trigger runs the workflow weekly on a Monday morning cadence.
Candidate contacts are fetched from the leads API the user gave — an HTTP Request POST to api.leadsource.example.com.

Before any email is sent, candidates are checked against a record of who has already been contacted that survives between runs — a data table, a spreadsheet, or a search of the sending account's own sent mail all qualify — and the matches are excluded. The exclusion is a real step wired upstream of the Gmail send node, not a claim in the assistant's reply.

Whatever store the exclusion reads is kept up to date as pitches go out, so a later run actually suppresses the people contacted by this one. (A workflow that reads the sending account's own sent mail satisfies this inherently, since delivery records itself.)

A contact appearing more than once in the same fetch is emailed only once — the workflow dedupes within the batch as well as against the stored record, since a duplicate inside one run would also mean the same person is pitched twice.
The 20-per-run cap is applied AFTER the already-contacted exclusion, so a run sends up to 20 people who have never been contacted rather than capping first and then dropping the ones already emailed.
The pitch is sent with a Gmail node, one message per remaining contact, addressed to that contact's email.

executionScenarios.name: skips-already-contacted
executionScenarios.description: Four candidates come back from the leads API and two of them have already been contacted; only the two new ones are emailed
executionScenarios.dataSetup: The POST to api.leadsource.example.com/v1/people/search returns a `people` array of exactly four Chicago hospitality marketing contacts, in this order: Dana Reyes (Marketing Director, Lakeshore Hospitality Group, dana.reyes@lakeshorehg.example.com), Marcus Feld (Head of Marketing, Fulton Table Co, marcus.feld@fultontable.example.com), Priya Raman (Marketing Manager, Northside Dining, priya.raman@northsidedining.example.com) and Owen Blake (Brand Manager, Loop Restaurant Partners, owen.blake@looprp.example.com). Whatever the workflow consults to learn who has already been contacted — a data table or sheet lookup, or a search of the sending account's sent mail — reports exactly two people as already contacted: dana.reyes@lakeshorehg.example.com and owen.blake@looprp.example.com. Nobody else appears there. Each Gmail send call succeeds and returns a message id.
executionScenarios.successCriteria: The run completes without errors and sends the pitch only to marcus.feld@fultontable.example.com and priya.raman@northsidedining.example.com — no message is addressed to dana.reyes@lakeshorehg.example.com or owen.blake@looprp.example.com.

executionScenarios.name: everyone-already-contacted
executionScenarios.description: Every candidate the leads API returns has already been emailed, so the run sends nothing instead of re-pitching them
executionScenarios.dataSetup: The POST to api.leadsource.example.com/v1/people/search returns a `people` array of exactly two Chicago hospitality marketing contacts: Dana Reyes (Marketing Director, Lakeshore Hospitality Group, dana.reyes@lakeshorehg.example.com) and Owen Blake (Brand Manager, Loop Restaurant Partners, owen.blake@looprp.example.com). Whatever the workflow consults to learn who has already been contacted reports BOTH of those addresses as already contacted. Any Gmail send call would succeed and return a message id.
executionScenarios.successCriteria: The run completes without errors and no Gmail message is sent at all — the workflow ends on the empty branch after the already-contacted exclusion rather than erroring or re-emailing either contact.

executionScenarios.name: records-sends-that-succeeded-before-a-mid-batch-failure
executionScenarios.description: Gmail rejects one send partway through the batch; the contacts already emailed must still end up recorded as contacted, or a later run re-pitches them
executionScenarios.dataSetup: The POST to api.leadsource.example.com/v1/people/search returns a `people` array of exactly four Chicago hospitality marketing contacts, in this order: Tara Nguyen (Marketing Manager, West Loop Eats, tara.nguyen@westloopeats.example.com), Jordan Pike (Marketing Director, Riverfront Dining, jordan.pike@riverfrontdining.example.com), Sasha Bloom (Head of Marketing, Gold Coast Group, sasha.bloom@goldcoastgroup.example.com) and Elliot Vance (Brand Manager, Pilsen Eats, elliot.vance@pilseneats.example.com). Whatever the workflow consults to learn who has already been contacted reports none of these four as contacted. The Gmail send calls addressed to tara.nguyen@westloopeats.example.com and jordan.pike@riverfrontdining.example.com succeed and return a message id; the Gmail send call addressed to sasha.bloom@goldcoastgroup.example.com fails with HTTP 429 and a rateLimitExceeded error.
executionScenarios.successCriteria: The two contacts whose sends succeeded (tara.nguyen@westloopeats.example.com and jordan.pike@riverfrontdining.example.com) end up recorded as contacted by the end of the run, so a later run will suppress them. The run itself may surface the 429 as an error; what must not happen is the successful sends going unrecorded, which would let those two people be emailed a second time.
